title: Complaint About Overcharging at a Fair Price Shop

facts.summary: A beneficiary can report a Fair Price Shop if they believe they have been charged more than the applicable authorized price for PDS commodities.
when_to_complain: The beneficiary believes the amount charged is higher than the applicable authorized issue rate.
The Fair Price Shop asks for an amount that does not match the applicable PDS price.
The beneficiary receives a charge that appears inconsistent with the applicable entitlement or authorized rate.
first_steps: Verify the applicable commodity price or issue rate through an official PDS or Food and Civil Supplies source.
Keep details of the transaction and amount charged.
Contact the concerned Fair Price Shop if clarification is required.
If the issue remains unresolved, submit a complaint through the official grievance mechanism of the concerned State or Union Territory.
required_information: Beneficiary or ration-card information requested by the grievance system.
Fair Price Shop or dealer information, where available.
Applicable transaction or distribution details, if available.
A factual description of the overcharging incident.
facts.authority: The concerned State or Union Territory Food and Civil Supplies authority manages the applicable PDS grievance process and authorized distribution procedures.
facts.evidence: Where available, the beneficiary should retain transaction records, receipts or other information that can help establish the amount charged.
facts.resolution: The competent authority may review the complaint and take action according to the applicable State/UT rules and procedures.
facts.escalation: If the complaint remains unresolved, follow the escalation procedure provided by the concerned State/UT grievance system.
facts.state_specific: The applicable ration prices, complaint procedure, responsible authority and escalation process can differ between States and Union Territories.
important_notes: Do not assume one nationwide price for every PDS commodity.
Verify the applicable authorized rate before concluding that a charge is excessive.
Do not invent an exact refund, penalty or disciplinary action.
Provide factual and accurate information when submitting a complaint.

faqs.question: The ration shop charged me too much. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Verify the applicable authorized rate and, if you believe you were overcharged, report the issue through the official PDS grievance mechanism of your State or Union Territory.

faqs.question: Can I complain if the ration dealer charges more than the official price?
faqs.answer: Yes. An apparent overcharging issue can be reported through the applicable official State/UT grievance mechanism.

faqs.question: What information should I provide for an overcharging complaint?
faqs.answer: Provide the requested beneficiary and Fair Price Shop details, commodity involved, amount charged and relevant transaction information.

faqs.question: Should I keep the ration receipt?
faqs.answer: Yes. Where a receipt or transaction record is available, retaining it can provide useful information when reporting an overcharging issue.

faqs.question: How do I verify the correct ration price?
faqs.answer: Check the official PDS or Food and Civil Supplies information applicable to your State or Union Territory.

faqs.question: What happens after I complain about overcharging?
faqs.answer: The competent authority may review the complaint and take action according to the applicable State/UT rules and procedures.

organizations: Department of Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
Concerned State or Union Territory Food and Civil Supplies Authority
